# 12 Resolve participant lifeline extents (create/destroy) and box groupings

## Outcome

`buildSequenceModel` computes each participant's real lifeline extent: start position = its
`create` statement's position if `origin: "created"`, else the diagram top; end position = its
`destroy` statement's position if one exists, else the diagram bottom. Box statements resolve
against the explicit-reference rule (every `participantIds` entry must be a validly declared
participant) and get stable `box-${n}` ids.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A participant declared via plain `participant`/`actor` (no `create`) with no `destroy`
  resolves with `createdAt: "top"`, `destroyedAt: "bottom"`.
- [ ] A participant declared via `create participant` resolves with `createdAt` equal to that
  statement's position; if never `destroy`ed, `destroyedAt: "bottom"`.
- [ ] A `destroy`ed participant resolves with `destroyedAt` equal to the `destroy` statement's
  position.
- [ ] A `destroy` referencing an id with no prior declaration/creation produces an error
  diagnostic (explicit-reference rule, same as messages).
- [ ] A second `destroy` on an already-destroyed participant produces an error diagnostic (a
  lifeline can only end once).
- [ ] A message referencing a participant *after* its resolved `destroyedAt` position produces a
  warning diagnostic (mirrors flowchart's "edge outlives its endpoint" warning in
  `buildGraphModel.ts` — same spirit, applied to sequence lifelines).
- [ ] Each `box` resolves with a stable id and its `participantIds` validated against declared
  participants; an unresolvable member id produces an error diagnostic.

## Test seam

`buildSequenceModel(document: SequenceDocument): { model: SequenceModel | null; diagnostics:
Diagnostic[] }` — unit level, pure function, extending ticket 07's test file with hand-built
create/destroy/box fixtures.
